title: Supercomputer Installs Take A Dive In The Second Half Of 2026
gist: Only 27 new machines entered the November 2026 Top500, the lowest churn since 1993; Timothy Prickett Morgan attributes the stall mainly to roadmap timing (Nvidia Rubin/Vera, AMD MI400/Venice, 1.6 Tb/sec networking in 2027) rather than a cloud shift. Nvidia Grace-based systems took 51.8% of new capacity, a China Telecom cloud cluster with Hygon/MetaX chips inflated core counts, and AMD's MI430X sets up a native-vs-emulated FP64 battle.

insights.claim: Only 27 new machines were added to the November 2026 Top500 supercomputer list, the lowest churn across all 68 Top500 lists compiled since 1993 and roughly half the normal number of new HPL-tested installs.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A record-low refresh rate signals a pause in on-prem HPC procurement that suppliers of HPC systems (HPE, Nvidia, AMD) may feel in near-term orders.
insights.quote: This is the lowest amount of churn across the 68 Top500 lists that have been compiled since 1993.

insights.claim: The collapse in new Top500 installations may reflect HPC buyers shifting toward renting cloud capacity instead of buying a new machine every four or five years and building ever-hotter, ever-more-expensive datacenters to house it.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: If the cloud-rental explanation wins out, on-prem HPC system vendors lose share to cloud providers; watch future lists to discriminate.
insights.locator: This is not a good sign

insights.claim: Timothy Prickett Morgan believes the November 2026 Top500 stall is mainly about roadmap timing — customers waiting on Nvidia Rubin/Vera and AMD MI400/Venice parts ramping in 2027 and on 1.6 Tb/sec networking — rather than a shift of HPC workloads to the cloud.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Treat the dip as deferred, not lost, HPC demand; expect a catch-up in 2027 installations tied to next-gen GPU and network ramps.
insights.quote: I still believe the stall is more about roadmap timing
insights.locator: All that said, I still believe

insights.claim: HPC networking is stuck at 800 Gb/sec ports while the market waits for 1.6 Tb/sec ports, which is contributing to delayed supercomputer installations.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: 1.6 Tb/sec switch/NIC availability is a gating item for the next HPC buildout wave — a catalyst to watch for networking suppliers.
insights.quote: particularly with networking, which is stalled at 800 Gb/sec ports when the world is expecting 1.6 Tb/sec ports
insights.locator: All that said, I still believe

insights.claim: About two dozen extra supercomputers would need to be installed across the June 2027, November 2027 and June 2028 Top500 lists to make up for the November 2026 shortfall; a light June 2027 list would require the following two lists to be above average.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Use the June 2027 new-install count as the test of the 'timing, not cloud' thesis.
insights.quote: I would expect about two dozen extra machines to be installed
insights.locator: We will see as the June 2027

insights.claim: The Top500 list caretakers (Erich Strohmaier, Jack Dongarra, Horst Simon) say the November 2026 results do not mean performance has stopped growing; a larger share of improvement is coming from additions and upgrades below the very top rather than wholesale replacement of leading machines.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: HPC spending is shifting toward incremental upgrades of existing systems rather than flagship replacements — favors upgrade/expansion revenue over big-bang deals.
insights.quote: a larger share of improvement is coming from additions and upgrades below the very top rather than from wholesale replacement of leading installations

themes.theme: CPU roadmap slips: Intel Diamond Rapids

insights.claim: Intel's 256 P-core Diamond Rapids Xeon 7 is rumored to debut in the second half of 2027 on Intel 18A-P, about a year late; the 16-memory-channel version is sampling, the mainstream 8-channel Diamond Rapids has been killed, and Granite Rapids Xeon 6+ will fill the gap until a future Xeon 8 refresh.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Intel's server CPU delay and cancelled mainstream SKU leave a gap in the 2027 HPC/server CPU cycle that AMD Venice can exploit.
insights.locator: Intel does not have an HPC-focused GPU

insights.claim: Intel does not have an HPC-focused GPU on the market, only GPUs aimed at inference, leaving HPC accelerator competition to Nvidia and AMD.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Intel is effectively absent from HPC accelerator share; the HPC GPU race is a two-horse Nvidia/AMD contest.
insights.quote: Intel does not have an HPC-focused GPU in the market
insights.locator: Intel does not have an HPC-focused GPU

themes.theme: Top500 as a skewed market proxy

insights.claim: The Top500 is a skewed view of the HPC market: it only includes machines that formally submit HPL results, while there are on the order of 3,000 proper HPC sites worldwide (excluding AI systems), many large machines never submit, and the middle and bottom of the list are padded with cloud, telecom and software-company clusters that do not do HPC as their day job.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Do not read Top500 counts as a market-size measure; use it as a signal of architectural choices only.
insights.quote: we get a skewed view of the HPC systems market

insights.claim: Tracking only new Top500 entrants (264 machines from June 2024 through November 2026), and eventually a rolling list of machines no older than four to five years, better reveals what HPC buyers are choosing than the full list, which is clogged with very old machinery as HPC centers stretch system lifetimes like hyperscalers do.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Lengthening HPC system lifetimes, like hyperscaler depreciation stretches, slow replacement cycles and vendor refresh revenue.

insights.claim: A China Telecom eSurfing Cloud IaaS cluster in Shanghai, built on 56-core Hygon C86 CPUs (derived from a licensed AMD Zen1 core) and MetaX C588 GPUs in two-CPU/eight-GPU nodes, accounted for 66.63 million of the 71.4 million cores across the 27 new November 2026 Top500 machines (93.3 percent) but only 2.9 percent of their aggregate Rpeak.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Chinese domestic accelerators (MetaX) are deployed at massive core counts but low per-chip performance — evidence of the capability gap export controls create.
insights.quote: This one “machine” on the cloud represented 93.3 percent of all of the cores
insights.locator: There is a China Telecom cloud

insights.claim: The China Telecom eSurfing Cloud cluster delivered only 38.66 petaflops peak and 18.36 petaflops sustained on HPL despite its huge core count, showing Chinese CPUs and GPUs are not particularly powerful compared to what is available in the United States.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Raw core counts overstate Chinese compute; ~47% HPL efficiency and low peak argue the US silicon lead remains wide.
insights.quote: None of them is particularly powerful compared to what is available in the United States
insights.locator: There is a China Telecom cloud

themes.theme: Largest new systems and vendor mix

insights.claim: The most powerful new November 2026 Top500 machine is KISTI's Hangang system in South Korea at 588.3 petaflops peak, built on Nvidia Grace-Hopper superchips in HPE Cray EX254n nodes with HPE Slingshot 400 interconnect.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: HPE plus Nvidia remain the default pairing for top national HPC wins.

insights.claim: Five Nvidia Grace-Hopper or Grace-Blackwell systems made up 51.8 percent (682.5 petaflops) of all new capacity added to the November 2026 Top500, out of just 1.32 exaflops aggregate Rpeak across all 27 new machines.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Nvidia's Arm-based superchips captured the majority of new HPC capacity in the cycle.

insights.claim: The second-largest new November 2026 Top500 system is Oak Ridge National Laboratory's Lux, rated at 323.9 petaflops, built on HPE ProLiant XD685 nodes with AMD Turin Epyc 9575F CPUs and Antares MI355X GPUs.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: AMD keeps winning DOE lab systems; HPE is the integrator on both of the two largest new machines.

insights.claim: On the November 2026 Top500, 290 of 500 machines (58 percent) use GPUs or other accelerators, accounting for 70.4 percent of total cores and 79.9 percent of total peak performance, versus 5.7 exaflops for CPU-only systems.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Accelerated computing dominates HPC flops; CPU-only HPC is a shrinking slice of capacity.
insights.quote: The accelerated systems comprise 58 percent of machines, but 70.4 percent of total cores on the list and 79.9 percent of total peak exaflops.

insights.claim: Nvidia GPU-based machines hold 52.9 percent of Top500 FP64 flops versus 37.7 percent for AMD GPUs, with AMD concentrated in a number of very large machines despite Nvidia having the lion's share of system count.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: AMD's flop share is far higher than its system count implies — it wins the biggest HPC deals.

insights.claim: AMD's MI430X, aimed explicitly at HPC with very high true FP64 performance, will ramp over the coming year and a half against Nvidia GPUs that rely on emulated, software-based FP64 atop matrix math engines, setting up a test of native versus emulated double precision.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: MI430X traction in 2027-2028 HPC deals is the key watch item for AMD share gains in ModSim versus Nvidia's AI-optimized parts.
insights.quote: Nvidia GPUs with emulated, software-based FP64 computing atop matrix math engines instead of true FP64 performance
